title: ICE buys robotic dogs from Connecticut company for patrols
source_used: CT Insider (Hearst Connecticut Media; read in full from the pre-fetched text)
key_facts: US Immigration and Customs Enforcement (ICE) is buying robotic 'dogs' for patrols, fitted with thermal, infrared and other sensors made by Radeco of Plainfield, Connecticut.
The photo caption says ICE is purchasing five robots similar to Boston Dynamics' Spot.
The Department of Homeland Security published the $1.3 million Radeco contract on Sam.gov, assigned to an ICE office in Orlando, Florida.

DHS says the robots would help staff with remote inspection, situational awareness and hazard assessment in unsafe, confined or hard-to-reach places, including detecting radiation, toxic gas and explosive threats, and checking oxygen levels in tunnels.
DHS says it got two responses from robotics companies in its market research and only Radeco met all specifications, including an arm reaching more than five feet.
Radeco's sensors and software are installed on Boston Dynamics' quadruped Cerberus and Spot robots; Radeco's president could not be reached.
Boston Dynamics says it will not sell its robots for uses that violate privacy and civil rights laws and has pledged not to sell robots equipped with weapons.
ICE agents have been active in Connecticut towns this summer and fall.
quote_evidence: The Department of Homeland Security published details of the $1.3 million Radeco contract on the Sam.gov website, with the purchase assigned to an ICE office in Orlando, Florida.
On its website, Boston Dynamics says it will not sell its robots for use in ways that violate privacy and civil rights laws.
Radeco sensors and software are installed on quadruped Cerberus and Spot robots from Boston Dynamics, which is based in Waltham, Massachusetts.
why_it_matters_hint: Immigration enforcement is adding robot dogs, which DHS describes as inspection tools for dangerous places.
event_date: Article 10 Oct 2026; date of the contract posting not stated
notes: The date the contract was posted on Sam.gov is not stated. The article's lede says 'patrols', while DHS's own stated purpose is inspection and hazard assessment; the summary keeps the DHS wording. The article is partly based on documents, which we did not open. Radeco did not comment.
